title: The Inter-State Council

endcard.line: Pictures: Ankur Panchbudhe from Pune, India (CC BY 2.0); unknown photographer (public domain)

segments.say: When the Centre and the States disagree, where do they sit down together? The Constitution's answer is in Article two sixty-three.
It lets the President set up an Inter-State Council by order, to look into disputes between States, study shared subjects, and recommend better coordination.
Article two sixty-three has been in the Constitution since nineteen fifty. The Council itself was set up by a Presidential Order in nineteen ninety, and was reconstituted in twenty fifteen.
The Prime Minister chairs it. Its members are the Chief Ministers of every State, the heads of Union Territories, and six Union ministers.
A smaller Standing Committee, chaired by the Home Minister, follows up on how the Council's decisions are carried out.
Don't confuse it with the Zonal Councils, which are headed by the Union Home Minister and bring together the States of one zone.
For GS Two, remember: Article two sixty-three, chaired by the Prime Minister, and it recommends rather than rules.

sources: Constitution of India, official English text (Legislative Department diglot PDF, legislative.gov.in, 'as on' 2024 edition): Art. 263 (President may establish an Inter-State Council by order, charged with inquiring into and advising on disputes between States, investigating subjects of common interest, and making recommendations for better coordination)

PIB, 17 December 2015 (relid 133519): ISC and its Standing Committee reconstituted under Clause 2 of the Inter-State Council Order, 1990; Chairman the Prime Minister; members Chief Ministers of all States, Chief Ministers of UTs with a legislature and Administrators of UTs without one, and six Union Ministers; Standing Committee chaired by the Home Minister, among its tasks to monitor the implementation of decisions taken on the Council's recommendations

MHA, Centre-State Division page: Zonal Councils are headed by the Union Home Minister with the Chief Ministers of the States in each zone; the Division handles Inter-State Council matters, including the Sarkaria Commission's recommendations

quiz.q: Under which Article can the President set up an Inter-State Council?

quiz.why: PIB 2015: Chairman, the Prime Minister. The Home Minister chairs the Standing Committee and the Zonal Councils.

quiz.q: The Inter-State Council was set up by…
quiz.why: PIB refers to the Inter-State Council Order, 1990.

reviewNote: Facts are from the Constitution, a 2015 PIB release and the MHA Centre-State page. The script does not say how often the Council has met, because no official count was read. It doesn't name the Sarkaria Commission in the voice-over; add it only with a source that links the 1990 order to it directly. Moving facts: the Council's membership is reconstituted from time to time.
